subject: High error spike / retry amplification — Neptune Analytics (urgent customer update)
messages:

Cc: support@neptuneanalytics.com

Marcus —

We've been seeing a huge increase in 5xx and 429s across our nightly batch jobs since 06:20 PT. Latency spikes to several seconds and some jobs are timing out. Our platform is heavy on short-lived bursts so this is killing throughput. We opened an internal ticket and our customers are already complaining.

Can you confirm: is this a Redwood-side regression? ETA to stabilize? We need an update to send to our SREs and our ops leadership in 30 minutes.

Attachments: sample request IDs + timestamps attached (error-logs-20261205.zip)

— Alicia
Head of Platform Engineering, Neptune Analytics

Alicia — quick update:

1) We see an elevated 5xx/429 rate correlated with a spike in retries originating from several high-volume tenants (including Neptune).
2) Initial hypothesis: a client-side SDK change plus a routing threshold interaction caused request amplification into a hotspot; our autoscaler is reacting but lagging under the burst pattern.
3) Action plan (immediate): throttling rule + temporary rate cap for noisy tenants, enable extra worker pool, and push a routing fix to avoid hot shards. ETA for first mitigation: 20–30 minutes. ETA to full normalization: 2–4 hours (depending on rollback and cache warmups).

I'm attaching our log bundle (error-logs-20261205.zip) and a 15-minute sample (rate-sample-20261205.csv) we pulled for your team.

I'll post a formal status note and update status.redwood.ai once throttles are live.

Marcus
Staff Engineer, Incident Response
Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai

Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-05T09:25:01-08:00
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Errors & timeouts across prod — immediate update requested

Marking internal steps completed / in progress:

- Rate cap (soft) applied to tenant group that included Neptune — currently throttling ~35% of requests from that group to reduce retry amplification.
- Extra worker pool spun up (3 x p4-equivalent) to absorb bursts; traffic steering in progress.
- Rolling back the recent SDK-congruent routing policy on the canary route to cut the hotspot; will push within 10 minutes.
- Alert added to SUP-9876 (see JIRA-INC-9876).

Note: we are intentionally avoiding a global rollback. We need to preserve throughput for unaffected tenants while stabilizing noisy flows.

Monica
Technical Ops Manager, Redwood Dedicated

> Marcus: please post a short customer-friendly update to Alicia with the ETA once throttles are confirmed. I'll coordinate the change window for the routing rollback.

Alicia — brief, customer-facing update for your SREs:

Hi Alicia — quick note from Redwood: we identified a spike in client retries that amplified traffic to a small set of serving shards and led to elevated 5xx/429s. We applied a targeted soft rate cap for noisy tenant groups and spun up additional workers. We are also rolling back a recent routing policy on the canary route that appears to have increased shard hotness.

ETA: throttles are live (09:35 PT). We expect visible error-rate improvement within the next 15–30 minutes and further stabilization as the rollback finishes (up to 3 hours for full traffic rebalancing).

We will post real-time status on https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-2026-1210 and escalate with you if anything changes.

If you'd like, we can schedule a postmortem call once things are stable.

— Marcus

> Monica: thanks for the rapid coordination.

Thanks Marcus — we've pulled the first set of telemetry and see error rates dropping from ~18% to ~7% after 09:35. That's a visible improvement.

Two asks:
1) Can your team add a short note to the status page explaining "targeted tenant throttles" so our customers understand why a small percentage of requests may get 429s now but system-wide timeouts are reduced?
2) Once you confirm the rollback is complete and rebalancing finished, please provide the definitive ETA for a postmortem and whether log-level traces from Redwood will be available to Neptune for the RCA.

Appreciate the rapid response — Alicia

Internal exec summary for record and follow-up:

- Incident ID: RED-2026-1210 (linked in related_links).
- Impact: transient elevated 5xx/429 across several high-volume tenants between 06:20–13:45 PT, peak error-rate ~21% for affected flows. Neptune Analytics experienced increased job failures and higher latencies; partial customer impact reported.
- Mitigations performed: targeted soft rate caps (09:35 PT), extra worker pool added (09:40 PT), canary routing rollback initiated (09:50 PT), final routing fix deployed (12:58 PT).
- Current status: error-rate for Neptune down to <1% for regular traffic patterns as of 14:10 PT; job throughput returning to normal.
- RCA timeline: Preliminary RCA will be shared within 48 hours. We will provide sanitized traces and the shard-mapping logs for Neptune under a data-sharing agreement; request for additional logs documented in SUP-9876.
- Next steps: schedule a joint postmortem with Neptune (preferred window Monday 12/7 or Tuesday 12/8), customer-facing incident summary to be posted to status.redwood.ai, and internal follow-up to harden routing thresholds and add early-detection alerts for rapid retry amplification.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-timeline-RED-2026-1210.pdf (uploaded to Jira), error-logs-20261205.zip
